oldDek: Cumberland crate habit, jazz/soul flips, jungle when the room can take it — and a 2am kettle that stays on.
newDek: Five Club Copy titles, three different genre lines, and a Cumberland address: what the pages actually say about L.T. Drifta.

oldDek: If Lions’ Gate was the crossing, L.T. Drifta’s Champion Sound is what happens once you’re inside and the afters become the point.
newDek: CC001 is one instrumental track, 4:53, dated 9 July 2024 on Bandcamp. The catalogue number and the public date agree.

oldDek: L.T. Drifta for a warm room when nobody wants to leave.
newDek: Eight short electronic tracks, released 14 November 2025. The Bandcamp sleeve times Summer Madness at 20:35.

oldDek: Vancouver house that stays after the room clears — smug until the drums lock at 3am with the kettle.
newDek: Forsberg's Bandcamp says Cumberland. The label page says Vancouver. The records are the part that does not depend on the line.

oldDek: Two tracks from Forsberg: windows cracked, city going violet, a passenger you haven’t figured out yet.
newDek: Two Forsberg tracks, 10 August 2026. Bandcamp times them 3:27 and 4:51. The sleeve credits CJ Archer as producer.

oldDek: Riscape’s first Club Copy EP is out: four tracks, digital live, cassette sold out.
newDek: Riscape's CC004: four house tracks, 15:02, released 18 September 2026. Bandcamp titles the last one Days Like This.

oldDek: The Athens producer making peak-time house that still has a tune — packed rooms, late nights, people who came to stay.
newDek: Athens, a conservatory, two Club Copy titles, and a chart claim the label bio states and this piece will not pretend to have rechecked.

oldDek: CJ Archer’s Club Copy beat tape — short instrumentals with the coat still on, fingerprints still on the samples.
newDek: A 22 August 2023 note announced a CJ Archer beat tape. The current Club Copy catalogue does not list one.

oldDek: One L.T. Drifta cut named for the bridge when the city says you’re not done — water under, email unfinished, night still open.
newDek: A 1 June 2024 note named a L.T. Drifta cut after the bridge. The current artist page does not list the title.

oldDek: L.T. Drifta, nine minutes. I played it twice before I looked at a clock.
newDek: The 30 August 2026 note reviewed a L.T. Drifta title the artist page's five-record list does not include.

oldDek: Vancouver, the weather, and why a finished record is usually a feeling somebody refused to throw away.
newDek: The 27 October 2022 conversation, kept as printed, and read against the catalogue the label actually released.

oldDek: Burial, rain on the glass, the club you could still hear from the kitchen.
newDek: Burial's second album, Hyperdub, 5 November 2007: garage slowed down until the walk home is the song.

oldDek: Björk, strings and beats: the record you put on when the kitchen wants to be weather.
newDek: Björk's third album, 1997, with Mark Bell and a string octet: beats and orchestra as the same weather.

oldDek: Put this on when your loops feel too clean, when everything lands on the grid like it was afraid to be late to its own party.
newDek: J Dilla's Donuts, Stones Throw, 7 February 2006: thirty-one short instrumentals, released three days before he died.

oldDek: Switzerland gave him a Rhodes, and he lived in it for a year.
newDek: Ahmad Jamal '73, on 20th Century Records: the trio's sense of space, moved onto electric piano.

oldDek: Still the door I send people through when they want a life out of other people’s records without being a tourist in them.
newDek: DJ Shadow's 1996 Mo' Wax debut: an album built from other people's records, and a method with a pulse.

oldDek: Portishead on a Cumberland afternoon, rain on the glass. I still start people here.
newDek: Portishead's debut, Go! Beat, 22 August 1994: a Bristol album that made the sample feel like a voice.

oldDek: Sakamoto, off the movie. I put it on when the apartment needs a temperature, not a plot.
newDek: Sakamoto, Byrne, and Cong Su scored The Last Emperor in 1987. The music holds up with the film turned off.

oldDek: Sade, 1992. The record I leave on when people are still in the apartment.
newDek: Sade's fourth album, Epic, 26 October 1992. Quiet, on this record, is a decision with a rhythm section under it.

oldDek: Nia Archives dropped Forbidden Feelingz: Bradford, Maya Angelou, and a tempo the field already missed.
newDek: Nia Archives' Forbidden Feelingz, on her label HIJINXX: Bradford, jungle tempo, and a title that names Maya Angelou.

oldDek: Eliza Rose took garage to the chart, and the booth already knew the chant.
newDek: Eliza Rose and Interplanetary Criminal's B.O.T.A.: a UK garage chant that reached the Top 10 with Lisa Lisa in the sample.

oldDek: Honey Dijon’s Black Girl Magic treats house like a family affair: Eve, the club, and a kick that doesn’t apologize.
newDek: Honey Dijon's Black Girl Magic, on Classic Music Company: a house album that casts guests without becoming a compilation.

oldDek: Eight tracks from a bedroom, and the floor already had the 2-step.
newDek: PinkPantheress, To Hell With It, October 2021: short songs, garage drums, a bedroom upload that became the record.

oldDek: Mary’s Underground threw a Lorde night, and then Lorde walked in and skipped the green room.
newDek: On 25 May 2025 Lorde stood in the crowd at Mary's Underground in Sydney for a night of her own song.

oldDek: DC’s Born I tours with Plum Village monks — bars over singing bowls, and a scene that still treats stillness like failure.
newDek: Born I, a DC producer, toured Hip Hop Soundbaths with Plum Village monastics. The album is called AMIDA.

oldDek: A tofu-delivery manga rewired a generation’s ear — eurobeat, an AE86, and a CRT glowing like a second moon.
newDek: Initial D paired a mountain pass with eurobeat. The soundtrack outlived the joke and taught a tempo what devotion sounds like.

oldDek: Wet shoes, no list, bin after bin — the side you’d play for someone you were trying not to impress.
newDek: Digging is a method, not a personality. The find is the record you almost put back, and the shop is not a moral stage.

oldDek: SOPHIE died in Athens. The oil didn’t dry.
newDek: SOPHIE died in Athens on 30 January 2021. The records, from BIPP to OIL OF EVERY PEARL'S UN-INSIDES, were already finished.

oldDek: Pressing plant is eighteen months out. Bandcamp Friday is not a vibe. It’s the object you can still hold.
newDek: In 2021 the pressing plants were backed up and Bandcamp Friday waived its cut. The copy you could pay for was a file.

oldDek: Wrapped is a brochure and For You is a corridor with no door, but the night still happens in a body.
newDek: A recommendation is a corridor. A room has a door, a night, and a person who decided the next record.

oldDek: AI can fake a finished song. It can’t fake the six months you disappeared into and came back with a bridge.
newDek: A model can imitate a finished track. It cannot supply the months a person disappeared into before the bridge existed.

oldDek: RA is a brochure and Dice is a receipt, but the night starts at 4:12 in a thread.
newDek: Resident Advisor lists the night and Dice sells the ticket. The address still moves the way it moved in 1998: person to person.

oldDek: The club photo is a lie with good lighting. The night starts when somebody puts a record on and nobody takes a vote.
newDek: The photograph is the brochure. The night that matters starts when someone plays a record and nobody votes on it.

oldDek: Physical is up 26%, and half the millennial CD buyers don’t own a player, but you still buy the thing you can hold.
newDek: Luminate's first-half-of-2026 figures said physical revenue was up 26 percent. The object came back. The reason to buy it did not change.

oldDek: The boys grade vinyl, and you kept the xerox that still smells like the room.
newDek: The flyer was the first pressing of the night: cheap paper, a date, and a record of a room that did not issue one.

oldDek: DICE sold the webcam to Superstruct, and the rooms are asking who owns the rectangle.
newDek: On 15 January 2025 DICE sold Boiler Room to Superstruct. The stream had a landlord. The night never had.

oldDek: Berghain is selling tickets. DJ Mag dropped them to 21. The door can still send you home.
newDek: In the 2026 DJ Mag poll Berghain placed 21st. A ticket, the club made clear, is not an admission.

oldDek: The Met still wants drill lyrics as evidence: 252 defendants in three years, and a verse is not a police report.
newDek: In September 2026 the Met defended drill lyrics as evidence. A report counted 252 defendants in three years.

oldDek: Nine people signed a petition to ban Hello Kitty pajama pants at raves, and the rooms that actually open are printing the cat on the flyer anyway.
newDek: Nine signatures on a 6 February 2026 petition tried to police pajama pants. The flyers were already printing the cat.

oldDek: On Thursday 15 October a timber shed with a corrugated roof turned up in Deep Sleep, 1,375 feet under Eryri, and the people who reached it were still wearing helmets. Roni Size played. The anthem went first. The record form is still unsigned.
newDek: On 15 October 2026 Roni Size played a timber booth 1,375 feet under a Welsh slate mine. The world-record claim went out as a submission.

oldDek: In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats puts you in a car, a service station and a 1989 acid house chase at Sensoria in Sheffield, the same week Amsterdam Dance Event turns 30.
newDek: In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats puts a visitor in a car, a service station, and a 1989 acid-house chase at Sensoria in Sheffield.

oldDek: On 7 October, in an interview with Highsnobiety, Jesper Kouthoofd said he is planning to stop making synthesizers, and that the OP-1 is included. He told the staff during a reorganization last autumn. The interview names no end date. On 15 October, DJ Mag wrote the plan up as an announcement.
newDek: On 7 October 2026 Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety he plans to stop making synthesizers, OP-1 included. DJ Mag wrote it up on 15 October.

oldDek: From 2008 to 2012 the Guvernment was eighth in the world. Toronto’s other night was a basement under the Silver Dollar, and a tent in a park.
newDek: From 2008 to 2012 the Guvernment was eighth in the world. Toronto’s other night was a basement under the Silver Dollar, and a tent in a park.
